title: Reading the first bit of a parse block
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x=\mathrm{pre}\,b\,\mathrm{rest}$ for Boolean words $\mathrm{pre},\mathrm{rest}$ and a bit $b$, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$. From the threaded-map parser's pair-reading state with emitting flag $e$, input head at position $|\mathrm{pre}|+1$, capture head at displacement $0$, and output $\mathrm{out}$, one step advances the input head to position $|\mathrm{pre}|+2$, records $b$ in the controller state, and appends $b$ to the output exactly when $e$ is true; the capture head remains at displacement $0$.
hypotheses_covered: M is a finite Boolean Turing machine
x equals pre followed by b and rest
pre and rest are Boolean words
c is an M-configuration on x
e is a Boolean emitting flag
replaced:
If the input splits as $x = p\, b\, s$ with bit $b$, one step of the
threaded-map controller from its block-start parse state at position
$\abs{p}$ records $b$ in the finite control and advances the input head,
emitting $b$ exactly when the controller is in its emitting (replay) pass.
